source.stem: By which process does oxygen pass out of a leaf?

packed_tags.subject: science
packed_tags.topic: What is living; diversity, life cycles and plant processes

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: Carbon dioxide + water -- in sunlight and chlorophyll --> starch + oxygen.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: With carbon dioxide, water, and chlorophyll, photosynthesis produces glucose and oxygen even in darkness.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Photosynthesis: glucose + oxygen -- in sunlight and chlorophyll --> carbon dioxide + water.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: Plant respiration also uses carbon dioxide and water in sunlight and chlorophyll to produce glucose and oxygen.

intelligence.enrichment: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll to produce glucose, and oxygen is released. Carbon dioxide + water -- in sunlight and chlorophyll -> glucose + oxygen. The learner correctly applies this rule: Photosynthesis uses carbon dioxide and water in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll to produce glucose, and oxygen is released. The photosynthesis equation is just plant food plus sunlight, and the named materials can be placed on either side.
